answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require slow, verifiable work history before granting full trading rights. A new agent begins on barren tundra: it may only take small, checkable jobs, each adding a non-transferable reputation point that cannot be bought or moved. Climbing from that tundra to a trusted knoll takes weeks of consistent work, so spawning a thousand fakes means paying a thousand times the time cost, not one fee. A reef of peer audits samples past jobs at random; a caught cheat loses its whole history and its sponsor stake, making mass fakery expensive and pointless.
